title: Continuum-refinement study for the one-dimensional defect benchmark
status_detail: Proposed fourth follow-on after the analytical oracle. No independently refined continuum comparison or crossover conclusion is active, calculated, or accepted.
objective: Determine whether lattice and parabolic defect observables approach a stable continuum comparison when grid spacing, domain length, supercell size, and defect width are refined independently.
authorized_scope: Plan frozen fixed-peak and fixed-integrated defect families with independently varied lattice scale, continuum discretization, domain length, supercell size, and profile width.
Track operator or compressed-operator residuals, bound-state counts, binding energies, equal-rank subspace fidelities, high-momentum weight, exterior residuals, and cross couplings separately.
Test a declared crossover criterion only after discretization, finite-domain, periodic-image, and profile-smoothness effects have been separated.
completion_criteria: Each claimed limiting trend is supported by at least one refinement axis that does not simultaneously change the physical profile or normalization convention.

Any proposed continuum crossover passes frozen exterior, cross-coupling, spectral, and wavefunction criteria and remains stable under the declared refinement sequence; otherwise no crossover is reported over the tested domain.
Deterministic inputs, independent verification, provenance, numerical limitations, and the absence of material validation or UQ are retained.
exclusions: Increasing profile width on one fixed grid is not sufficient to establish a continuum limit.
Fixed-peak and fixed-integrated families must not be combined into one convergence sequence.
No silicon, dopant, DFT, production Wannier, external execution, scientific validation, uncertainty quantification, or public API freeze is authorized.
